paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: a real faith is something you train, and it's built on what God has said, not on what people pile on top of it. Paul warns that in later times some will abandon the faith and follow deceitful spirits (1 Timothy 4:1). They will prohibit marriage and require abstinence from certain foods, but "every creation of God is good, and nothing that is received with thanksgiving should be rejected" (1 Timothy 4:4). So when somebody slaps a NO sign on what God made good, I think that's your cue to stop and check it against His Word.

Then Paul says, "train yourself for godliness" (1 Timothy 4:7). He says physical exercise is "of limited value," but godliness is "valuable in every way, holding promise for the present life and for the one to come" (1 Timothy 4:8). Limited is not none, friend, so go ahead and stay active, but don't put all your energy into the one workout that stops at the grave! The reason we labor and strive is that we have "set our hope on the living God, who is the Savior of everyone, and especially of those who believe" (1 Timothy 4:10).

And this training is for everybody, not just the pros. Timothy was young, and Paul still told him to set an example in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith and in purity (1 Timothy 4:12). He told him to devote himself to Scripture, not neglect his gift, and "pay close attention to your life and to your teaching" (1 Timothy 4:13-16). So, baker, whatever your age, you're not too young or too late, so keep showing up, keep your eyes on the Word, and let your progress be evident to all. I'll keep the ovens warm!
